nonblocking_findings_retained.note: Retained without concealment or downgrade. Not remediated in Phase A or Phase B. No .gitattributes change, no EOL normalization, no blob-hash migration.

post_publication_findings.substance: After lawful Phase-A publication, two lifecycle-sensitive assertions in tests/test_21g_u06_r3_substitution_attacks.py fail: test_untracked_r3_artifacts_are_not_published_in_head (2 subtests) and test_arbitrary_ancestor_is_not_proof_for_a_file_absent_there. Both hard-code the pre-publication premise that the R3 candidate checkpoint and src/production_authority_lifecycle_u06.py are untracked and therefore absent from any published commit, and assert that publication proofs must fail. Phase-A publication necessarily falsified that premise. In all three cases the validator behaved correctly: require_published_in_head and require_published_in_commit now succeed because the artifacts are genuinely published in commit 6677e1e7bff4e344f1d220de2c107b1e4d407d25.
post_publication_findings.mechanical_blocking_determination: NOT A PHASE-B ACCEPTANCE BLOCKER. Determined from the live lifecycle architecture, not by waiver: no production or lifecycle module executes tests or consults any test result; VALIDATION_IDENTITY_PATHS is consumed only by validation_identity() and runtime_dependency_report(), which hash files for read-only reporting; tests_are_runtime_production_authority is false; and neither the acceptance_closure nor the acceptance_manifest role contract references test state.
post_publication_findings.a01_core_attack_suite_status: The core A-01 substitution attacks, including the auditor's exact five-artifact attack using real tracked published artifacts, still pass. 29 of 31 test_21g cases pass.
post_publication_findings.disposition: DOCUMENTED NONBLOCKING POST-PUBLICATION FINDING, carried forward for the next independent auditor to adjudicate. Not remediated and not waived in this pass.
